name: Ultimate Flea
teaser: Full flea control for SPT 4.1: manage the item pool, set prices, pull Tarkov.dev averages, and run a local supply/demand economy with early-wipe scaling.
description:
UltimateFlea

Server-side flea market mod for SPT 4.1 (optional BepInEx client for level-lock UI).

Control what can be sold, set prices yourself, pull live averages from Tarkov.dev, run a local supply/demand economy with early-wipe scaling, and lock buy/sell by level like live T*****.

Buy me a coffee

Features
  • Item pool — blacklist / whitelist by item ID or category
  • Pricing — fixed prices, global/item/category multipliers
  • Tarkov.dev prices — uses avg24hPrice from json.tarkov.dev (with cache fallback)
  • Local economy — buys raise demand, sold player offers raise supply
  • Early wipe — temporary price multiplier based on character age (RegistrationDate)
  • Player offers only — optional flea with no virtual FakePlayer offers and no trader listings
  • Level locks — buy/sell gated by level (live-like table in levels.json); server enforces even without the client
  • WTT-friendly — can unblacklist custom items so they appear on the flea

Configured through JSON. Optional client plugin for lock icon / level labels / tooltips.

Install
  1. Extract the archive into the SPT game folder (next to EscapeFromTarkov.exe), overwrite files
  2. Edit configs in SPT_Runtime/user/mods/UltimateFlea/config/
  3. Start the server (and client if you installed the BepInEx plugin)

What the zip installs:

  • SPT_Runtime/user/mods/UltimateFlea/ — server mod
  • BepInEx/plugins/UltimateFlea/ — optional client plugin

Default configs use a local price preset (SPT handbook / prices.json) plus soft early-wipe and light events. Level locks ship enabled with a live-like table.

Config
File Purpose
mod.json Master switches, price source, flea behavior
pool.json What can / cannot be listed
pricing.json Fixed prices and multipliers
economy.json Supply/demand simulation and wipe settings
events.json Timed category/item multipliers by wipe day
trends.json Optional slow category price waves
levels.json Level locks for buy/sell (live-like defaults)

Item IDs: https://db.sp-tushonka.com/ or offline list in the repo: https://github.com/SVAR316/UltimateFlea/blob/main/docs/ITEM_IDS.md

Economy state is saved to data/economy_state.json. Tarkov.dev prices are cached under data/ as well.

How to configure

Edit JSON files in SPT_Runtime/user/mods/UltimateFlea/config/, then restart the server (restart the client too if you changed level-lock UI behavior).

Quick start

  1. Default preset is local prices + soft early-wipe + light category events.
  2. Set "priceSource": "tarkovdev" only if you want live Tarkov.dev averages. Then turn off wipe / events / trends, or prices will stack above live.
  3. Use pool.json only if you want to force-add/remove items. Pool rules affect the flea only — they do not strip PMC loot.
  4. Use pricing.json for fixed prices or multipliers.
  5. Tune economy.json if prices move too fast/slow or wipe feels too strong.
  6. Optional: enable trends.json for slow category waves.
  7. Optional: "playerOffersOnly": true for player listings only.
  8. Level locks: levels.json (enabled, items, categories). Server blocks buy/sell below level; client plugin improves the UI.
  9. After big economy changes, delete data/economy_state.json for a clean start.

Trader assort prices are not changed by this mod.

mod.json

Field What it does
enabled Turns the whole mod on/off
enablePoolManager Enables pool add/remove rules
enablePricing Enables custom price rules
enableEconomy Enables supply/demand simulation
priceSource local (default) or tarkovdev
pvePrices If using tarkovdev: use PvE prices instead of regular
preserveBasePrices Stops SPT from rebuilding prices from handbook
disableTraderPriceFloor Allows flea prices below trader buy prices
exactOfferPrices Removes SPT’s 0.8–1.2 offer price spread (affects whole flea)
playerOffersOnly Only real player listings (no virtual offers, no trader flea listings)
debug Extra logging

pool.json

Field What it does
mode blacklist or whitelist
add / remove Specific item TPLs
addCategories / removeCategories Direct parent category IDs
  • Blacklist: keeps the normal SPT pool and only changes listed items/categories.
  • Whitelist: only items in add / addCategories are allowed; everything else is blocked.
  • Item rules beat category rules.
  • If WTT blacklists a custom item, putting it in add also clears that blacklist/cache so offers can spawn.

pricing.json

Field What it does
globalMultiplier Multiplies all prices
fixedPrices Hard RUB price by item TPL; economy never changes these
itemMultipliers Multiplier by item TPL
categoryMultipliers Multiplier by parent category

Get item TPLs from https://db.sp-tushonka.com/ (24-char ID, not the item name).

Example: lock Graphics card to 200000 RUB forever:

{
  "globalMultiplier": 1.0,
  "fixedPrices": {
    "57347ca924597744596b4e71": 200000
  },
  "itemMultipliers": {},
  "categoryMultipliers": {}
}

If you only want it a bit more expensive, use itemMultipliers instead, e.g. "57347ca924597744596b4e71": 1.5.
Make sure "enablePricing": true in mod.json. Restart the server after edits.

economy.json

Field What it does
simIntervalMinutes Minutes between economy ticks
demandPerBuy Demand added when buying from flea
supplyPerSell Supply added when a player offer sells
priceElasticity How hard supply/demand push the target price
decayPerTick How fast demand/supply fade each tick
settleSpeed How quickly current price moves toward the target
noise Random market noise around the target
minPriceFactor / maxPriceFactor Floor/ceiling vs base price
wipe.enabled Early-wipe multiplier (default on for local)
wipe.startLengthDays How long the expensive early-wipe phase lasts
wipe.startMultiplier Multiplier on day 0; fades to 1.0 by the end

Wipe age uses the character’s RegistrationDate, not mod install time. With multiple profiles, the oldest PMC is used.

events.json

Timed category/item multipliers by wipe day. Default local preset includes light hideout / ammo / late-barter events.

Field What it does
enabled Turns events on/off
events[].id Label for logs
events[].startDay / endDay Wipe-age window (endDay exclusive)
events[].multiplier Price multiplier while active
events[].categories Parent category IDs
events[].items Specific item TPLs

Several matching active events multiply together.

trends.json

Optional slow sine-wave drifts by category. Off by default.

Field What it does
enabled Turns trends on/off
trends[].category Parent category ID
trends[].periodDays Full wave length in days
trends[].amplitude Peak +/- deviation from 1.0 (clamped 0..0.5)
trends[].phase Phase offset in radians

Target price each tick:

base * wipe * events * trends * (1 + supply/demand pressure + noise)

levels.json

Level-locked flea trading (buy and/or sell), similar to live T*****.

Field What it does
enabled Turns level locks on/off
useSptDefaults Start from SPT tieredFlea levels, then apply your overrides
lockBuying Block buying player offers below the required level
lockSelling Block listing items below the required level
items Item TPL -> required level (0 removes a lock)
categories Category / base class ID -> required level (0 removes a lock)

Priority: ammo tier / exact item / highest matching category. Trader offers are never locked by this.

Without the client plugin, the server still rejects illegal buy/sell. With the client plugin you also get locked offer UI, level tooltips, and category labels with the flea lock icon.

FIKA

Server mod — install on the host only.
Client plugin — install on every client that should see the level-lock UI.
I haven’t tested it extensively with FIKA, but there should be no architecture conflict.

Planned
  • Better client UI parity with live flea locks (edge cases)
Bugs

Open an issue on GitHub: https://github.com/SVAR316/UltimateFlea/issues
